title: Elodie and the Ledger Revisited
premise: Freya Eastwick, a night-shift dispatcher for Halcyon Cabs, receives a confession letter for a murder committed thirty years ago — postmarked the day after the victim's funeral, and naming Freya's own mother as an accomplice. Following the ledger of fares recorded that night in 1994, Freya discovers the 'dead' witness, taxi driver Marcus Vale, may have faked his death and is still driving routes under another name. As she closes in, Freya learns the town's founding family buried the truth to protect a fortune built on stolen land. In the end, Freya finds Marcus alive but dying, extracts his testimony, and chooses to publish it — trading her own sense of belonging in the town for the memory of those erased.
about_author: R. M. Quintana is the pen name of a former small-town court reporter who spent a decade transcribing confessions before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about paper trails, quiet towns, and the people who keep everyone else's secrets.

chapters.title: The Postmark
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. On a slow night shift, Freya opens a confession letter describing a 1994 hit-and-run — postmarked the day after the victim's funeral last week. The letter names her late mother as a witness. Emotional beat: unease disguised as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: Night Shift Rules
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Establishing routine at Halcyon Cabs; Freya's pride in closing every case, her isolation since her mother's death. She cross-references the letter against old dispatch logs and finds page torn from the 1994 ledger. Beat: stubborn resolve.

chapters.title: The Funeral She Missed
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya attends the victim's belated memorial and observes the grieving Wren family, whose patriarch died last week — the letter's victim. A daughter, Imogen Wren, watches Freya too closely. Beat: first sense of being watched.

chapters.title: Ledger Ghosts
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In the archive basement, Freya finds the 1994 fare ledger: three trips logged the night of the accident, one signed by driver Marcus Vale — officially dead since 2001. Beat: thrill of the hunt curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears He's Dead
chapters.summary: Freya interviews retired dispatcher Dolores, who insists she saw Vale's body after the 'accident' at Miller's Bend. Dolores warns Freya off with genuine fear. Beat: the town closes ranks.

chapters.title: Imogen
chapters.summary: Imogen Wren's POV. The heiress privately hires Freya to find the letter-writer, claiming the confession is blackmail. Her grief seems rehearsed. Beat: seductive alliance with something rotten underneath.

chapters.title: Miller's Bend
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya walks the crash site at dawn and finds a fresh cigarette butt and tire tracks — someone still visits. A passing driver recognizes her mother's maiden name and goes pale. Beat: the past is not past.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Another letter arrives, this one addressed to Freya by name: 'Your mother kept the ledger honest. Don't let them keep you dishonest.' It includes a partial cab number. Beat: personal stakes ignite.

chapters.title: Routes and Routines
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Cross-referencing current dispatch data, Freya notices a veteran driver, 'Sam Okafor,' whose routes eerily mirror Vale's old patterns. She begins tailing him between fares. Beat: hunter becoming hunted.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Sam Okafor's POV. Sam — Marcus Vale — knows he's being followed and debates running again. Flashbacks reveal he witnessed the Wrens' fixer kill a journalist in 1994 and has been hiding ever since. Beat: hunted tenderness.

chapters.title: Convergence at the Depot
chapters.summary: Freya confronts Sam in the depot garage; he denies everything until she recites the ledger entry verbatim. He gives her twenty-four hours and a key to a bus locker. Beat: wary truce.

chapters.title: Locker 12
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The locker holds her mother's handwriting: annotated ledger pages proving the Wrens paid off police, plus a photo of young Freya — her mother knew everything and stayed silent to protect her. Beat: betrayal and love entangled.

chapters.title: Dolores Breaks
chapters.summary: Dolores's POV. Pressured by an anonymous caller, Dolores confesses to Freya that she helped fake Vale's death in 2001 at the mother's request. Beat: guilt finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: The Wren Fortune
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Research reveals the Wren empire was built on land seized after the 1994 scandal killed the journalist investigating it. The confession letter wasn't remorse — it was leverage. Beat: power's architecture exposed.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Someone runs Freya's cab off the road near Miller's Bend. She survives, but her apartment is searched and the ledger pages gone. Beat: fear becomes fury.

chapters.title: Imogen's Offer
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Imogen offers Freya money and belonging — a place in the Wren orbit — if she returns what her mother left. Her vulnerability is real but her loyalty to the family name wins. Beat: temptation with a human face.

chapters.title: What Mother Knew
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Reconstructing her mother's notes, Freya realizes her mother wrote the original confession letters years ago and mailed the final one from her deathbed arrangement — postdated. The funeral timing was coincidence weaponized by whoever intercepted it. Beat: grief reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Dead Witness Rides Again
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. Sam decides to testify, knowing the Wrens' fixer — now the town's police chief — will come for him. He records his full account and mails copies. Beat: courage after thirty years of flight.

chapters.title: Chief Corliss
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Confronted, Chief Corliss admits the cover-up but claims he protected the town, not just the Wrens — jobs, pensions, order. He offers Freya her mother's silence as precedent. Beat: the banality of corruption.

chapters.title: Miller's Bend, Again
chapters.summary: Freya and Sam's POV alternating. At the crash site, Corliss corners them; Imogen arrives unexpectedly and, hearing the full truth of her father's crime, turns on the chief instead. Standoff resolves when Sam's mailed recordings surface. Beat: climax — truth outguns power.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Sam testifies before state investigators; the Wren holdings unravel; Imogen cooperates to dismantle rather than defend the legacy. Freya is offered her old life back and declines quietly. Beat: cost acknowledged.

chapters.title: Open Ledger
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya closes the ledger case, pins the final letter above her dispatch desk, and takes the morning shift for the first time — no longer hiding from daylight or the town. Belonging rebuilt on truth, not silence. Beat: resolution and quiet hope.
